definition: Firebase Studio (formerly known as Project IDX) is an online integrated development environment (IDE) developed by Google.
details: It is based on Visual Studio Code, and the infrastructure runs on Google Cloud. In addition to including the features, languages and plugins supported by VS Code, it has unique functionality built by Google. These include a built-in generative AI assistant powered by Gemini, Nix integrations, and Android emulators. Google also provides templates for JavaScript, Python, and Go projects, as well for as a number of web and cross-platform frameworks such as Node, Angular, Flutter, Next.js, React, FireBase, Google Maps, and Flask. The application was initially only accessible after signing up on a waitlist. It was released as an open beta on May 14, 2024. It was renamed from Project IDX to Firebase Studio on April 15, 2025. In March 2026, Google announced that the service would be discontinued in March 2027, in order to focus on other AI development tools.

explainer.lead: Firebase Studio is Google's online development workspace for writing and testing applications without setting up the whole toolchain locally. It combines a Visual Studio Code-based editor, cloud infrastructure, project templates, Android emulators, and a Gemini-powered coding assistant. Google announced in March 2026 that it would discontinue the service in March 2027 to focus on other AI development tools.

tiers.eli5: Firebase Studio is like a ready-to-use workshop for making apps on the internet. Instead of buying and arranging every tool yourself, you pick a project template and get an editor, a place to run your work, and an AI helper. It was first called Project IDX before becoming Firebase Studio.
tiers.practitioner: Start from a JavaScript, Python, or Go template, or use a framework setup such as Next.js, React, Angular, Flutter, Node, or Flask. The VS Code-based environment runs on Google Cloud, with Nix integrations, Gemini assistance, and Android emulators available alongside familiar VS Code languages and plugins. Plan for migration because Google has announced discontinuation in March 2027.
tiers.paperLevel: Firebase Studio is a cloud-hosted integrated development environment built on Visual Studio Code and Google Cloud, augmented with Gemini-based generative AI, Nix integration, framework templates, and Android emulation. It was released as an open beta on May 14, 2024, and renamed from Project IDX on April 15, 2025. Its announced lifecycle ends with discontinuation in March 2027.

explainer.example: A developer can start a Flutter project from a template, edit it in the VS Code-based workspace, ask Gemini for help with the code, and test the app in an Android emulator without installing that full setup on a local computer.

usedIn.name: Web application development
usedIn.detail: Templates cover frameworks including Angular, Next.js, React, and Node.

usedIn.name: Cross-platform app development
usedIn.detail: Flutter templates and Android emulators support building and testing apps.

usedIn.name: Backend and cloud projects
usedIn.detail: Python, Go, JavaScript, and Flask templates run in a Google Cloud-hosted workspace.

explainer.intuition: It packages the pieces needed to begin coding into one online workspace. Rather than configuring an editor, dependencies, framework tooling, and an emulator separately, a developer starts with a prepared environment and can ask Gemini for assistance while working.
howItWorks: Open the online IDE and choose a language or framework template.
Write code in the Visual Studio Code-based editor, using its supported languages and plugins.
Run the workspace on Google Cloud, with Nix integrations supporting the environment.
Use the built-in Gemini assistant for generative AI help during development.
Test Android-related work with the provided emulators.
explainer.whyItMatters: Firebase Studio shows how generative AI can be embedded directly into a cloud development environment rather than offered only as a separate chat tool. Its templates and managed infrastructure reduce initial setup, while its announced shutdown highlights the migration risk of depending on a hosted service.
misconceptions: It is not an editor built entirely from scratch: it is based on Visual Studio Code.
It is not only a Gemini chat interface: it also provides an IDE, templates, cloud infrastructure, Nix integrations, and Android emulators.
Its open-beta release and its renaming were separate events, occurring on May 14, 2024, and April 15, 2025.
